title: Independently check #4439/#4442: halo exponents 12, 26, 28, 28, 6 under eps = 1/(16p^2) (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds `research/eps-halo-exponent-check/`. It is an independent check of jwr404's #4439 (within one cell) and #4442 (across cells, downward reading), the halo exponents under the relative budget `ε = 1/(16p²)`. It is the ε-route counterpart of my #4460.

**Claim type:** an independent check by separate code, with exact rationals. **No new κ.**

## Results

All statements check out.

- **Ceiling.** The split identity (grid-proved) gives `off ≤ (16p²−2)/(16p²−1)`, so the gap is exactly `1/(16p²−1)`.
- **Exponents.** Endpoint 12, length 26, bandwidth and agreement 28, normalizer 6 (7 also works), exact for `p` in 2..64, with all-`p` arguments.
- **Fails.** 11 and 5 at `p = 2`; 25 at `p = 2` (certified); 27 at `p = 2` (loose count) and for `p ≥ 3` (sharp count).
- **#4442's extras.** The `p = 2` tightness `63·63 > 62·64` and the bare-kernel example (square gap 32/16 against 20/16) both hold.

## Evidence

```text
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eps-halo-exponent-check --check-only
  PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eps-halo-exponent-check
  PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/eps-halo-exponent-check outcome=completed   (<1 s, stdlib only)
```
